newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya's Moi to hold Africa conflict summit.
newsitem.headline: Kenya's Moi to hold Africa conflict summit.

text.p: Kenya's President Daniel arap Moi announced on Friday he would convene an African summit in March on conflict resolutions in the volatile region.

"President Moi announced that a major summit will be held in Nairobi on March 12 this year to discuss conflict resolutions in various parts of Africa," Moi said in a statement issued by the Presidential Press Service.
There were no details on the summit's focus or which countries might attend.

Moi is currently involved in a peace initiative over the war in Zaire, where rebels have seized control of a swath of territory around 1,000 km (600 miles) long in the east prompting a counter-offensive by government forces.
Kenya's Foreign Minister Kalonzo Musyoka returned on Thursday with the foreign ministers of South Africa and Tanzania from a mission to Kinshasa.
They said Zaire demanded a total withdrawal of foreign forces from eastern Zaire before it would attend a proposed summit in Nairobi on the conflict. Zaire boycotted two earlier summits in Nairobi.
South Africa is holding talks this week towards a face-to-face meeting between Zaire rebels and the government.
